Load Data

airbnb_boston <- read_csv("~/Desktop/airbnb_boston-2.csv")
## Rows: 2997 Columns: 10
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (3): property_type, room_type, neighbourhood
## dbl (7): price, reviews_per_month, accommodates, bathrooms, bedrooms, beds, ...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
airbnb_boston = airbnb_boston %>%
na.omit()
airbnb_boston = airbnb_boston %>%
select(price, neighbourhood, property_type)

Exercise 1

Part a

# Asked ChatGPT for color codes below
boston_palette <- c("#003f5c", "#ffa600", "#bc5090", "#58508d")

airbnb_boston_treemap <- airbnb_boston %>%
  treemap(
    index = c("property_type", "neighbourhood"),
    vSize = "price",
    vColor = "price",
    palette = boston_palette,
    title = "Boston Airbnb Prices by Property Type and Neighborhood")

Part b

d3tree_Boston <- d3tree(airbnb_boston_treemap)
d3tree_Boston

Exercise 2

a

neighborhood_filtered <- airbnb_boston %>%
  filter(neighbourhood %in% c("Fenway", "East Boston", 
                             "Roxbury", "West Roxbury",
                             "Hyde Park", "Dorchester", 
                            "Allston", "Back Bay"))

# In Canva it said my dataset was too big, so I took out Allston

head(neighborhood_filtered)
## # A tibble: 6 × 3
##   price neighbourhood property_type
##   <dbl> <chr>         <chr>        
## 1   125 East Boston   Apartment    
## 2   145 Roxbury       Other        
## 3   169 Roxbury       Other        
## 4   179 Back Bay      Apartment    
## 5   154 Dorchester    Apartment    
## 6   115 Back Bay      Other
write.csv(neighborhood_filtered, "neighborhood_filtered.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Further analysis

# Decided to take out "Other" from property_type so that the data would fit Canva
neighborhood_filtered_2 <- airbnb_boston %>%
  filter(neighbourhood %in% c("Fenway", "East Boston", 
                              "Roxbury", "West Roxbury",
                              "Hyde Park", "Dorchester", 
                              "Allston", "Back Bay") &
         property_type != "Other")

# The data was still too big, so I chose include anything priced over 50

neighborhood_filtered_3 <- airbnb_boston %>%
  filter(neighbourhood %in% c("Fenway", "East Boston", 
                         "Roxbury", "West Roxbury",
                         "Hyde Park", "Dorchester", 
                         "Allston", "Back Bay") &
    property_type != "Other" &
    price > 50)

write.csv(neighborhood_filtered_3, "neighborhood_filtered_3.csv", row.names = FALSE)
